title: I Accidentally Became the person responsible for an impossible prophecy and Everything Went Wrong
synopsis: A dungeon manager tries to reduce adventurer complaints while an ancient evil keeps filing maintenance requests. The story unfolds in The Archipelago of Suspiciously Convenient Prophecies, where prophecies become stronger when people misunderstand them. The central problem is a celestial committee preparing an audit of mortal civilization. Mira Bell wants to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot, but every reasonable solution creates a new unreasonable obligation.
premise: A dungeon manager tries to reduce adventurer complaints while an ancient evil keeps filing maintenance requests.
authorNotes: The original outline had twelve chapters. Then somebody discovered a receipt.

chapters.title: I Regret Discovering the Prophecy Problem — Mira Bell POV
chapters.arcTitle: The Problem With The Original Plan
paragraphs: CHAPTER 1 — Mira Bell POV
The Problem With The Original Plan had already produced two meetings, one argument, and a document nobody could legally throw away.
Mira Bell arrived at the abandoned academy intending to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot. The plan lasted until the first unexpected detail appeared.
Someone admits that they knew more than they claimed.
Mira Bell regarded the situation with the professional disappointment of someone who had already predicted it.
The important object was a umbrella. It was not magical in the usual sense, which made it considerably more suspicious.
Mira Bell checked the obvious explanation first. It was wrong. They checked the ridiculous explanation next. It was unfortunately closer.
The world of The Archipelago of Suspiciously Convenient Prophecies followed one inconvenient rule: Prophecies become stronger when people misunderstand them.
The conversation became quieter when everyone realized that the newest clue had a date older than the kingdom itself.
This was technically progress. Unfortunately, it was progress in the wrong direction.
A second person arrived carrying information about the identity of the person who altered history. Their explanation contradicted the first explanation in exactly the way a useful clue should.
Nobody agreed on what to do with the umbrella. One person wanted to destroy it. Another wanted to file it. Mira Bell wanted to know why it had appeared here.
That question led to a small discovery: Mira Bell has a private connection to the oldest dungeon.
The mystery remained open, although Mira Bell now had one useful fact: someone was treating the identity of the person who altered history as if it were a normal administrative matter.
Before leaving, Mira Bell made a decision that would matter later: they would not trust the next official document until they had read the footnotes.
For the first time that day, everyone agreed on something. This was probably going to get worse.
